p: A few quick tips before you head in. Bring photo ID if there's any chance you look under 25, as bar-led venues commonly ask. Book your lane before the weekend if you're coming in a group, and think about how many lanes you need. A gang of eight or more will have a much better time across two lanes than squeezed onto one.

If you're coming by train, Bristol Temple Meads is around a 15 to 20 minute walk away, or a short bus ride. Bus routes into Broadmead are plentiful too, which is handy if you're planning on a drink or two and want to leave the car at home. Cabot Circus has a large car park if you do need to drive, though it can fill up on busy Saturdays.

Union Street is also well placed for a pre-bowl wander through some of Bristol's older corners. Castle Park, just to the south, has the ruins of St Peter's Church, bombed in the Blitz and now kept as a memorial, alongside the remains of Bristol Castle. The Christmas Steps, a steep, narrow lane of little shops, is a short walk west and is one of the city's most charming streets.
Theatre fans can catch a show at the Bristol Old Vic on King Street, which dates back to the 1760s, and still be back in time for a late game. It's a cracking area for packing a lot into one evening.
